To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

acute exposure of rats to carbon disulide causes an increase in ATP content, accompanied by a decrease in ADP and AMP content in the brain, which may be related to the ultrastructure of mitochondrion.
acute and chronic exposure of rats to low concentrations of CS2 results in an increased concentration of ATP in the cerebrum and in the ultrastructural changes in the cerebellum, respectively.

chronic exposure to carbon disulide did not affect the content of high-energy phosphate compounds and the ultrastructure of brain mitochondria, but acute poisoning with CS2 resulted in a significant increase of the brain ATP content accompanied by a significant decrease of AMP and ultrastructural alterations of mitochondria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of CS2 on the brain energy metabolism and ultrastructure of the mitochondria of the brain cells of rats exposed to CS2.
the biochemical and ultrastructural changes in the brain of animals exposed to CS2.
the effects of CS2 on the content of high-energy phosphate compounds and ultrastructure of the brain mitochondria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CS2 is a toxic substance which can induce changes in the brain ultrastructure, and that the biochemical and morphological changes are not necessarily related.
the biochemical and structural changes in the brain of acutely poisoned rats are not a result of the direct toxic action of CS2, but are due to the action of some other metabolites of CS2.

acute exposure to CS2 results in a significant increase in ATP content in brain tissue, which is accompanied by ultrastructural mitochondrial changes, whereas chronic exposure to CS2 does not result in changes in the content of high-energy phosphate compounds or in ultrastructural mitochondrial changes in brain tissue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

chronic exposure to carbon disulffide (CS2), even at concentrations below the occupational limit, may lead to a decrease in brain energy production, and that acute exposure may result in an increase in the content of ATP and a decrease in the content AMP.
the changes in ATP content and the ultrastructure of mitochondira are the result of acute intoxication with carbon disulphid.
the brain of rats is more sensitive to CS2 than the liver and that the brain is more sensitive after acute exposure than after chronic exposure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chronic exposure of animals to CS2 does not cause changes in the content of high-energy phosphate compounds in the brain.
the content of high-energy compounds in the brain and the structure of mitochondria are sensitive markers for acute and chronic exposure to carbon disulffide.
the brain is not resistant to CS2, and that the brain mitochondria may play an important role in the development of the toxic effects of CS2.
